key_insight: Pauli correlation encoding turns large combinatorial optimization into a compact variational quantum problem by representing binary choices with multi-body Pauli expectation values, enabling near-optimal solutions with very few qubits.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable quantum optimization framework for power-demand portfolio planning, where high-quality decisions can be obtained under strict qubit and hardware constraints.
method: Encode binary variables as Pauli correlation expectation values to create a continuous relaxation of the discrete objective.
Use a two-stage hybrid workflow: solve a time-averaged problem first, then initialize a time-resolved optimization.
Map the continuous output back to discrete solutions, with performance tied to correlator resolution and discretization quality.
evidence_signal: Simulations across problem sizes from m = 18 to 10,296 achieved normalized cost gaps around 10^-4 relative to certified-optimal solutions, and trapped-ion hardware tests remained robust under noise and finite sampling.
watch_item: Solution quality depends on how reliably improvements in the continuous relaxation translate into discrete gains, so correlator resolution and measurement noise can limit practical performance.
paper_title: Scalable Variational Quantum Optimization via Pauli Correlation Encoding: Application to Large-Scale Power Demand Portfolio Optimization
